title: dropdown chooser
name: Dropdown chooser — Tidwell
rule: For a bounded choice set, let the user pick from a drop-down chooser rather than typing the value from memory.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Drop-down Chooser (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Bounded set is picked from a drop-down (or equivalent chooser), not typed from memory.
fail_when: Bounded list is a blank the user must recall.
overview: Let users pick bounded values from a drop-down instead of typing from memory.
apply_when: Bounded choice sets where recalling the exact string is unnecessary.
not_when: Open values with no fixed list to choose from.
agent_hint: Use a drop-down chooser for bounded sets; do not force memory typing.
description: For a bounded choice set, let the user pick from a drop-down chooser rather than typing the value from memory. Pass when the bounded set is chosen from a drop-down or equivalent; fail when a bounded list is presented as a blank the user must recall. Prefer choosers that surface the options over memory-taxing free text.
